source.title: Stable Rank Normalization for Improved Generalization in Neural Networks and GANs
source.authors: Amartya Sanyal; P. Torr; P. Dokania

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some results relevant to randomized labels appear only in figures.
record.tranche_reason: The paper runs randomized-label shattering experiments and reports training performance, but does not test the claim’s full recipe or its test-error-at-chance component in a directly comparable way.
record.gate_note: The paper’s shattering experiments on randomized labels bear on V1 and partly on V5. Clean-label accuracy results do not test V1’s random-label claim and are not included as rows. Results cited from Zhang et al. (2016) are not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study performs the original random-label shattering test using SGD and training accuracy/error, while varying normalization, architecture, learning rate and weight decay.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that SRN reduces random-label memorization while improving clean classification and empirical generalization measures. This does not establish that standard networks generally cannot memorize random labels or that SRN preserves all clean-data fitting capacity.
record.recipe_differences: The study modifies the normalization of linear layers with SRN and compares it with spectral normalization and vanilla training; it does not reproduce the original studies’ full shattering protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: Random-label training outcomes vary with normalization method, architecture, learning rate, and weight decay; the authors also report that VGG-19 required lowering its learning rate to learn random labels.
record.problems: Random-label results in Figure 3 are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text. Table 1 and Table 6 label their values training error while saying higher is better, and the prose describes lower train error; this makes the numeric direction unclear. The experiments focus on SRN versus SN and vanilla training, not a direct replication of all claim conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant numeric results were left out. Other randomized-label results for CIFAR10 are shown only in Figure 11; the text says SRN-50 and SRN-30 are much better than Vanilla and SN, but gives no model-specific values or clear metric direction, so no further row was added.

untested.parts: Random-label test accuracy near 1% is stated in Section 5.2, but model-specific test results are not supplied. Most figure endpoints are unavailable; random-label runs use twice the clean-label training epochs, and VGG changes its learning rate.
Time to comparable fitting accuracy and convergence across corruption fractions are not established. Allocating twice as many epochs does not measure the required time overhead.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs is not tested.
No corruption-fraction sweep establishes perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error.
Dropout and data augmentation are not isolated. Clean-label removal results concern weight decay only; eventual random-label fitting beyond the reported stopping budgets is untested.
The study does not establish the temporal ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noise.

missing.what: VGG-19 failed to learn random labels at initial learning rate 0.1; the authors reduced it to 0.01 for shattering experiments.

Clean-label weight-decay removal comparison: vanilla test accuracy 69.2 ± 0.5 without versus 70.4 ± 0.3 with weight decay. Add method-specific rows. The surrounding heading identifies CIFAR100, while the caption says CIFAR10 and inconsistently describes the learning rate.
missing.locator: Appendix D.1, Table 7 and preceding paragraph

missing.what: AlexNet reportedly fails to learn clean data completely without weight decay at learning rate 0.1, providing a contrasting condition for the regularizer-removal claim. No absolute result is readable in the supplied figure text.
missing.locator: Appendix D.1, Alexnet experiments and Figure 6

missing.what: AlexNet random-label training-error comparison with and without weight decay at learning rate 0.01 is omitted; the prose states that stronger stable-rank constraints decrease fitting.
missing.locator: Appendix D.1, Figure 7a and accompanying text

record.verdict_notes: Training-error captions, numerical ordering and the repeated interpretation of higher error as less memorization support reading Tables 1 and 6 as errors despite the contradictory sentence in Section 5.2. Missing figure values cannot justify verdicts about absolute fitting. CIFAR10 Figure 11 is already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports randomized-label training performance, but does not establish for its models the complete combination of near-zero training error, test error at chance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters relative to clean-label training.
Training-time overhead and convergence speed as label corruption increases are not reported.
Shuffled-pixel and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
The study does not sweep corruption fractions from none to all or report the corresponding test-error trend.

The study compares weight decay settings for randomized-label fitting in selected settings. It does not test dropout or data augmentation, nor whether removing regularizers by itself harms generalization on true labels.
The study does not track whether true-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.
